You exchange AnonCreds credentials over DIDComm, with Issue Credential v2 and Present Proof v2. This page issues a credential and requests a proof with a predicate, then covers revocation. The AnonCreds specification calls the holder the prover when it presents. Both agents need the AnonCredsModule with a registry, and the issuer needs a registered credential definition: see AnonCreds.

The AnonCreds format services are exported from @credo-ts/anoncreds/didcomm since Credo 0.7.2. @credo-ts/anoncreds still exports them too, but those exports are deprecated and removed in 0.8. Register the services on both the credentials and the proofs protocol. agent.ts import { AnonCredsModule } from '@credo-ts/anoncreds' import { AnonCredsDidCommCredentialFormatService, AnonCredsDidCommProofFormatService, LegacyIndyDidCommCredentialFormatService, LegacyIndyDidCommProofFormatService, } from '@credo-ts/anoncreds/didcomm' import { CheqdDidRegistrar, CheqdDidResolver, CheqdModule } from '@credo-ts/cheqd' import { CheqdAnonCredsRegistry } from '@credo-ts/cheqd/anoncreds' import { Agent, DidsModule } from '@credo-ts/core' import { DidCommAutoAcceptCredential, DidCommAutoAcceptProof, DidCommCredentialEventTypes, DidCommCredentialState, type DidCommCredentialStateChangedEvent, DidCommCredentialV2Protocol, DidCommHttpOutboundTransport, DidCommModule, DidCommProofEventTypes, DidCommProofState, type DidCommProofStateChangedEvent, DidCommProofV2Protocol, } from '@credo-ts/didcomm' import { agentDependencies, DidCommHttpInboundTransport } from '@credo-ts/node' import { NativeAnoncreds } from '@hyperledger/anoncreds-nodejs' function createAgent(port: number, storage: ExampleStorage) { return new Agent({ dependencies: agentDependencies, modules: { ...storage, // Storage and key management, see Agent setup // The registry and its DID module, see the AnonCreds page cheqd: new CheqdModule({ networks: [{ network: 'testnet', cosmosPayerSeed: '<cosmos payer seed>' }] }), dids: new DidsModule({ registrars: [new CheqdDidRegistrar()], resolvers: [new CheqdDidResolver()] }), anoncreds: new AnonCredsModule({ anoncreds: NativeAnoncreds, registries: [new CheqdAnonCredsRegistry()] }), didcomm: new DidCommModule({ endpoints: [`http://localhost:${port}`], transports: { inbound: [new DidCommHttpInboundTransport({ port })], outbound: [new DidCommHttpOutboundTransport()], }, connections: { autoAcceptConnections: true }, credentials: { autoAcceptCredentials: DidCommAutoAcceptCredential.ContentApproved, credentialProtocols: [ new DidCommCredentialV2Protocol({ credentialFormats: [ new AnonCredsDidCommCredentialFormatService(), new LegacyIndyDidCommCredentialFormatService(), ], }), ], }, proofs: { autoAcceptProofs: DidCommAutoAcceptProof.ContentApproved, proofProtocols: [ new DidCommProofV2Protocol({ proofFormats: [new AnonCredsDidCommProofFormatService(), new LegacyIndyDidCommProofFormatService()], }), ], }, }), }, }) } There are two formats for the same credentials. anoncreds uses the AnonCreds attachments of RFC 0771. indy uses the older Hyperledger Indy attachments of RFC 0592, which some agents still require. Their API options are the same, under the anoncreds or indy key. The deprecated Issue Credential v1 and Present Proof v1 protocols only support the indy format, see Issuing credentials.

Issuer issuer.ts await issuer.didcomm.credentials.offerCredential({ connectionId, protocolVersion: 'v2', credentialFormats: { anoncreds: { credentialDefinitionId, // Values are strings, also for numbers you want to use in predicates attributes: [ { name: 'name', value: 'Jane Doe' }, { name: 'role', value: 'Developer' }, { name: 'age', value: '32' }, ], }, }, }) The attribute names must match the schema of the credential definition exactly: no missing and no extra attributes. AnonCreds values are strings. Predicates work on attributes whose value is an integer string. Holder holder.ts holder.events.on<DidCommCredentialStateChangedEvent>( DidCommCredentialEventTypes.DidCommCredentialStateChanged, async ({ payload: { credentialExchangeRecord } }) => { if (credentialExchangeRecord.state !== DidCommCredentialState.OfferReceived) return // The attribute names and values to show to the user console.log(credentialExchangeRecord.credentialAttributes) // Uses the default link secret, and creates it if there is none yet await holder.didcomm.credentials.acceptOffer({ credentialExchangeRecordId: credentialExchangeRecord.id }) } ) The holder binds the credential to its link secret. Credo creates a default link secret on the first credential request if there is none. To use another one, create it with agent.modules.anoncreds.createLinkSecret and pass credentialFormats: { anoncreds: { linkSecretId } } to acceptOffer. The holder stores the credential as a W3C credential record. AnonCreds shows how to query it.

Verifier verifier.ts await issuer.didcomm.proofs.requestProof({ connectionId, protocolVersion: 'v2', proofFormats: { anoncreds: { name: 'Employee check', version: '1.0', requested_attributes: { name: { name: 'name', restrictions: [{ cred_def_id: credentialDefinitionId }] }, role: { name: 'role', restrictions: [{ cred_def_id: credentialDefinitionId }] }, }, requested_predicates: { // Proves age >= 18 without revealing the age adult: { name: 'age', p_type: '>=', p_value: 18, restrictions: [{ cred_def_id: credentialDefinitionId }] }, }, }, }, }) The keys of requested_attributes and requested_predicates (name, role, adult) are referents: names you choose to find the values in the presentation. Use names: ['name', 'role'] instead of name to require attributes from the same credential. A predicate (>=, >, <= or < with an integer p_value) proves a comparison without revealing the value. Credo generates the nonce of the request when you leave it out. restrictions decide which credentials qualify, for example by cred_def_id, issuer_id or schema_id. Without restrictions, the holder can use any credential with that attribute, including one it issued itself, so restrict every item to the issuers you trust. Holder holder.ts holder.events.on<DidCommProofStateChangedEvent>( DidCommProofEventTypes.ProofStateChanged, async ({ payload: { proofRecord } }) => { if (proofRecord.state !== DidCommProofState.RequestReceived) return // Lists all matching credentials per attribute and predicate, to let the user choose const { proofFormats: options } = await holder.didcomm.proofs.getCredentialsForRequest({ proofExchangeRecordId: proofRecord.id, }) console.log(options.anoncreds?.attributes) // Or let Credo pick the first match for each const { proofFormats } = await holder.didcomm.proofs.selectCredentialsForRequest({ proofExchangeRecordId: proofRecord.id, }) await holder.didcomm.proofs.acceptRequest({ proofExchangeRecordId: proofRecord.id, proofFormats }) } ) All credentials in one presentation must be bound to the same link secret. Verifier verifier.ts issuer.events.on<DidCommProofStateChangedEvent>( DidCommProofEventTypes.ProofStateChanged, async ({ payload: { proofRecord } }) => { if (proofRecord.state !== DidCommProofState.PresentationReceived) return // Only valid presentations reach this state, so `proofRecord.isVerified` is true const { presentation } = await issuer.didcomm.proofs.getFormatData(proofRecord.id) const revealedAttributes = presentation?.anoncreds?.requested_proof.revealed_attrs ?? {} for (const [referent, { raw }] of Object.entries(revealedAttributes)) { console.log(referent, raw) } } ) The presentation contains the revealed attribute values under their referents. Predicates appear only as proven, without the value.

Revocation needs a revocable credential definition with a revocation registry and status list. AnonCreds shows how to create them and how to revoke. When you issue a revocable credential, pass the revocation registry and an index in it. Credo doesn't track which indexes you used: each credential needs its own, and you need the index later to revoke the credential. Issuer issuer.ts await issuer.didcomm.credentials.offerCredential({ connectionId, protocolVersion: 'v2', credentialFormats: { anoncreds: { credentialDefinitionId: revocableCredentialDefinitionId, attributes: [ { name: 'name', value: 'Jane Doe' }, { name: 'role', value: 'Developer' }, { name: 'age', value: '32' }, ], revocationRegistryDefinitionId, // Track which indexes you used, each credential needs its own revocationRegistryIndex: 1, }, }, }) After you revoke a credential, you can tell the holder with a revocation notification. The holder agent emits a DidCommCredentialEventTypes.DidCommRevocationNotificationReceived event and stores the notification on the exchange record (revocationNotification). Issuer issuer.ts // After revoking index 1 with updateRevocationStatusList, optionally notify the holder await issuer.didcomm.credentials.sendRevocationNotification({ connectionId, revocationFormat: 'anoncreds', revocationId: `${revocationRegistryDefinitionId}::1`, }) A verifier that wants proof that a credential isn't revoked sets non_revoked, on the whole request or per attribute or predicate. Set to, the time in seconds. If you also set from, it must equal to. Verifier verifier.ts await issuer.didcomm.proofs.requestProof({ connectionId, protocolVersion: 'v2', proofFormats: { anoncreds: { name: 'Employee check', version: '1.0', // Require a proof that the credential was not revoked at this time (seconds) non_revoked: { to: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) }, requested_attributes: { name: { name: 'name', restrictions: [{ cred_def_id: revocableCredentialDefinitionId }] }, }, }, }, }) The holder fetches the status list for that time from the registry. selectCredentialsForRequest skips revoked credentials, and throws when no valid credential is left.

The Data Integrity format can also issue AnonCreds credentials as W3C VCDM 1.1 credentials: offer with anonCredsLinkSecretBinding: { credentialDefinitionId } and bindingRequired: true, and register the AnonCredsModule on both agents. The offered credential may only contain @context, type, issuer, issuanceDate or validFrom, and credentialSubject, and type must be ['VerifiableCredential']. Present these credentials with DIF Presentation Exchange.

A DIDComm connection links two agents through a pair of DIDs, one for each side. Most DIDComm protocols run over a connection. This page covers invitations, connection states and events, and reusing connections.

One agent, the inviter, creates an out-of-band invitation and shares it as a URL or QR code. The other agent, the invitee, receives it and runs the DID Exchange protocol with the inviter. The examples on this page run Acme and Bob as two Node.js agents that reach each other over HTTP: connections.ts import { Agent } from '@credo-ts/core' import { DidCommConnectionEventTypes, type DidCommConnectionStateChangedEvent, DidCommDidExchangeState, DidCommHttpOutboundTransport, DidCommModule, } from '@credo-ts/didcomm' import { agentDependencies, DidCommHttpInboundTransport } from '@credo-ts/node' function createAgent(port: number, storage: ExampleStorage) { return new Agent({ dependencies: agentDependencies, modules: { ...storage, // Storage and key management, see Agent setup didcomm: new DidCommModule({ endpoints: [`http://localhost:${port}`], transports: { inbound: [new DidCommHttpInboundTransport({ port })], outbound: [new DidCommHttpOutboundTransport()], }, connections: { autoAcceptConnections: true }, }), }, }) } const acme = createAgent(4042, acmeStorage) const bob = createAgent(4043, bobStorage) await acme.initialize() await bob.initialize() With autoAcceptConnections: true, the inviter accepts DID Exchange requests automatically. On the invitee side, receiving an invitation accepts it by default. Accept requests manually shows how to approve each request yourself.

Invitation Use it when Out-of-band invitation You show a link or QR code to one user, for example during a web session. This is the default. Multi-use invitation You print or publish one QR code for everyone. Each invitee gets its own connection. Connectionless, with handshake: false and messages You only want to issue one credential or request one proof, without keeping a connection. See Issuing credentials and Requesting proofs. Invitation with a public DID Returning users should reuse their existing connection instead of creating a new one. Implicit invitation The invitee already knows your public DID and connects without an invitation. You accept each request manually. With DID Exchange, each side of the connection uses a new did:peer that only the other party knows, so connections with different parties can't be linked. A public DID, such as a did:web, only identifies the inviter in the invitation. You need one only to reuse connections or to accept implicit invitations.

acme.ts const outOfBandRecord = await acme.didcomm.oob.createInvitation({ label: 'Acme' }) const invitationUrl = outOfBandRecord.outOfBandInvitation.toUrl({ domain: 'https://acme.example.com/invite' }) toUrl() encodes the invitation in the oob query parameter of the URL you pass as domain. Use a domain you control. Render the URL as a QR code with any QR code library. Long invitations make dense QR codes. You can also share a short URL: when an invitation URL has no oob parameter, Credo fetches it and accepts either a JSON response with the invitation, or a redirect to the full invitation URL. createInvitation() options you may need: Option Description label Name shown to the invitee. alias Name for the connection in your own records. imageUrl Image shown to the invitee. goalCode, goal What the connection is for. multiUseInvitation Let more than one agent use the invitation. See Multi-use invitations. autoAcceptConnection Override autoAcceptConnections for this invitation. messages Attach a message, such as a credential offer or proof request, to the invitation. See Issuing credentials and Requesting proofs. handshake Set to false to only send the attached messages, without creating a connection. invitationDid Use an existing DID instead of a new key in the invitation. See Reuse a connection. routing Route the connection through a specific mediator. See Mediation.

bob.ts const invitation = await bob.didcomm.oob.parseInvitation(invitationUrl) console.log(`Bob received an invitation from ${invitation.label}`) const { connectionRecord } = await bob.didcomm.oob.receiveInvitation(invitation, { label: 'Bob' }) if (!connectionRecord) throw new Error('The invitation has no handshake protocols') const bobToAcme = await bob.didcomm.connections.returnWhenIsConnected(connectionRecord.id) parseInvitation() decodes the URL so you can show the invitation to the user before accepting it. receiveInvitation() then starts DID Exchange. To do both in one call, use receiveInvitationFromUrl(url, config). label is required: it is the name the inviter sees for you. Other options: Option Default Description alias Name for the connection in your own records. autoAcceptInvitation true Start DID Exchange right away. If false, call agent.didcomm.oob.acceptInvitation(outOfBandRecord.id, { label }) later. autoAcceptConnection true Complete the connection when the response arrives. If false, call agent.didcomm.connections.acceptResponse(connectionId). reuseConnection false Use an existing connection with the inviter if there is one. See Reuse a connection. routing default mediator Route the connection through a specific mediator. returnWhenIsConnected() waits until the connection reaches the completed state, for up to 20 seconds unless you pass { timeoutMs }. Credo parses oob invitation URLs, c_i URLs from the deprecated Connections protocol, and legacy connectionless d_m URLs. An agent can't receive the same invitation twice: the second attempt throws.

Each connection is a DidCommConnectionRecord with a state from DidCommDidExchangeState: State Side Meaning invitation-received Invitee Connection created, request not sent yet. request-sent Invitee Waiting for the inviter's response. request-received Inviter Waiting for you to accept the request, unless auto-accept is on. response-sent Inviter Response sent, waiting for the invitee to complete. response-received Invitee Waiting for you to accept the response, unless auto-accept is on. completed Both The connection is ready. The inviter has no connection record until the first request arrives. Listen for connection state changes and filter on the out-of-band record to react to connections from a specific invitation: acme.ts acme.events.on<DidCommConnectionStateChangedEvent>( DidCommConnectionEventTypes.DidCommConnectionStateChanged, ({ payload: { connectionRecord } }) => { if (connectionRecord.outOfBandId !== outOfBandRecord.id) return if (connectionRecord.state === DidCommDidExchangeState.Completed) { console.log(`Acme is connected with ${connectionRecord.theirLabel}`) } } ) To look up the connections an invitation created, use findAllByOutOfBandId(): acme.ts const [acmeToBob] = await acme.didcomm.connections.findAllByOutOfBandId(outOfBandRecord.id) await acme.didcomm.connections.returnWhenIsConnected(acmeToBob.id) The out-of-band record has its own state (DidCommOutOfBandState: initial, await-response, prepare-response, done) and emits DidCommOutOfBandEventTypes.OutOfBandStateChanged.

Create the invitation with autoAcceptConnection: false, or leave autoAcceptConnections off in the module config. Then accept each request when it arrives: acme.ts acme.events.on<DidCommConnectionStateChangedEvent>( DidCommConnectionEventTypes.DidCommConnectionStateChanged, async ({ payload: { connectionRecord } }) => { if (connectionRecord.state !== DidCommDidExchangeState.RequestReceived) return // Requests from implicit invitations, or from invitations created with autoAcceptConnection: false if (connectionRecord.autoAcceptConnection) return await acme.didcomm.connections.acceptRequest(connectionRecord.id) } ) Requests from implicit invitations always need this step.

A regular invitation creates one connection. A multi-use invitation stays valid, and every agent that uses it gets its own connection. Use it for invitations you print or publish, like a QR code on a website. acme.ts const multiUseRecord = await acme.didcomm.oob.createInvitation({ label: 'Acme', multiUseInvitation: true }) const multiUseUrl = multiUseRecord.outOfBandInvitation.toUrl({ domain: 'https://acme.example.com/invite' }) After Carol and Dave each receive the invitation: acme.ts const multiUseConnections = await acme.didcomm.connections.findAllByOutOfBandId(multiUseRecord.id) console.log(`The multi-use invitation created ${multiUseConnections.length} connections`) You can't attach messages to a multi-use invitation.

When an inviter puts the same DID in all of its invitations, an invitee that is already connected can reuse that connection instead of creating a new one. The inviter sets invitationDid, usually a public DID with a DIDComm service in its DID document (see DIDs): acme.ts // A DID that Acme created, with a DIDComm service in its DID document const publicDid = 'did:web:acme.example.com' const outOfBandRecord = await acme.didcomm.oob.createInvitation({ label: 'Acme', invitationDid: publicDid }) const invitationUrl = outOfBandRecord.outOfBandInvitation.toUrl({ domain: 'https://acme.example.com/invite' }) The invitee passes reuseConnection: true. If it has a connection with that DID, Credo sends a handshake reuse message over it and returns the existing connection: bob.ts const { connectionRecord } = await bob.didcomm.oob.receiveInvitationFromUrl(invitationUrl, { label: 'Bob', reuseConnection: true, }) The inviter learns about the reuse through an event: acme.ts acme.events.on<DidCommHandshakeReusedEvent>(DidCommOutOfBandEventTypes.HandshakeReused, ({ payload }) => { console.log(`${payload.connectionRecord.theirLabel} reused connection ${payload.connectionRecord.id}`) }) Invitations without invitationDid contain a new key each time, so Credo never matches them to an existing connection.

If you know an agent's public DID, you can connect without an invitation. Credo builds the invitation from the DIDComm services in the DID document: bob.ts const { connectionRecord: bobToAcme } = await bob.didcomm.oob.receiveImplicitInvitation({ did: publicDid, label: 'Bob', }) did can also be a DID URL that points to one service, for example did:web:acme.example.com#didcomm. The inviter must have created the DID in its own agent, and it accepts the request manually: Credo never accepts requests from implicit invitations automatically.

Deprecated The Connections 1.0 protocol (RFC 0160) is deprecated and removed in Credo 0.8. Use out-of-band invitations with DID Exchange. createInvitation() lists both DID Exchange and Connections 1.0 as handshake protocols, with DID Exchange first. To offer only DID Exchange, pass handshakeProtocols: [DidCommHandshakeProtocol.DidExchange]. Agents that only support the Connections protocol need a c_i invitation: acme.ts const { invitation } = await acme.didcomm.oob.createLegacyInvitation({ label: 'Acme' }) const invitationUrl = invitation.toUrl({ domain: 'https://acme.example.com/invite' })

Method on agent.didcomm.connections Description sendPing(connectionId) Send a trust ping to check that the other agent is reachable. rotate({ connectionId }) Switch to a new DID for this connection and tell the other agent (DID Rotate). hangup({ connectionId, deleteAfterHangup }) Tell the other agent the connection is over. With deleteAfterHangup: true, Credo also deletes the record. deleteById(connectionId) Delete the connection record without notifying the other agent. findAllByQuery(query) Find connections, for example by state or theirDid.

Issuing credentials Issue a credential over a connection. Requesting proofs Request and verify a presentation. Messaging Send basic messages and use other protocols. Mediation Reach mobile agents through a mediator.
