This is an internal change, but Askar now only uses short-lived sessions. Before a session was created and kept alive until the agent was shutdown or the tenant session was closed (in case of multi-tenancy). Now a session is created for each read and write operation to your wallet. Askar manages a connection pool internally and aligns more with how Askar is supposed to be used, and makes the multi-tenancy implementation more robust. This is also in preparation for some bigger wallet and storage API changes in future versions, where we want to support transactions (batching multiple read/writes operations), record locking (to prevent race condition updates), and more. See Pull Request 1743 for more information.

AnonCreds credentials in Credo now support the W3c Verifiable Credential format. Using the new Aries RFC 0809: W3C Verifiable Credential Data Integrity Attachment format you can issue AnonCreds credentials in W3C VC Data Integrity format, and verify them in W3C VC Data Integrity using Aries RFC 0510: Presentation-Exchange Attachment format. With the change, we've updated the storage of all AnonCreds credentials to be stored as W3cCredentialRecord instead of AnonCredsCredentialRecord. The AnonCredsCredentialRecord is still used for some legacy records which we were not able to migrate to the new format yes (because they rely on resolving objects from the ledger to properly migrate). However in future versions, also these records will be migrated and the AnonCredsCredentialRecord will be removed from the codebase. This means some AnonCreds credentials are stored in W3cCredentialRecord format, and some in AnonCredsCredentialRecord format. Make sure to use the designated methods on the AnonCredsModule as well as on the ProofsModule to find and query for AnonCreds records, to make sure all record types are returned. See Pull Request 1744 for more information.

This document describes everything you need to know for updating Credo 0.5.x to 0.6.x. If you're not aware of how updating in Credo works make sure to first read the guide on Updating Credo. First of all, update your dependencies to the 0.6.x versions. This will also update the needed peer dependencies. Extension packages are not updated with this command. You need to update these manually, and make sure they're up to date with the latest version of Credo. Credo 0.6.0 is a major release with a large number of breaking changes. The most notable ones are: ESM-only: Credo is now a pure ESM package. CommonJS require() is only supported in Node.JS 20.19 and above. But we recommend updating your project to ESM. DIDComm extracted from core: All DIDComm-related functionality has been moved to the new @credo-ts/didcomm package. New KMS API: The wallet API has been completely rewritten. agent.wallet is replaced by agent.kms. Wallet config moved: walletConfig has been removed from the main agent config and moved to the Askar module's store property. Askar dependency renamed: @hyperledger/aries-askar-* packages have been replaced by @openwallet-foundation/askar-*. label and connectionImageUrl removed from agent configuration. did:peer:4 is now the default for DID Exchange requests. Node 18 deprecated: Node 20 and 22 are now the supported versions. Follow the mentioned steps in this document carefully to make the upgrade as smooth as possible. caution The migration guide only covers how to migrate from 0.5.x to 0.6.x while keeping the same behavior and dependencies. There are many new features in 0.6.0 (Drizzle ORM storage, batch credentials, DCQL, W3C VCDM 2.0, etc.) that are not covered here. Refer to the release notes and the individual package changelogs for more information on new features. caution The automatic backup functionality has been removed from Credo 0.6.0. You are expected to create a backup yourself before performing any updates. For Askar you can export a store using the Askar API, or you can directly create a backup of your Postgres database. First install the updated dependencies. For all dependencies you have in package.json, update them to the following versions, for your platform. If you don't use a package, you don't have to add it here. In the upgrade from 0.5 to 0.6, there is a new @credo-ts/didcomm package that must be added if your application uses DIDComm. Also, the Askar native bindings have been moved from @hyperledger to @openwallet-foundation scope, so @hyperledger/aries-askar-* should be replaced by @openwallet-foundation/askar-*. React Native Node "@credo-ts/core": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/didcomm": "^0.6.0" (new, required if using DIDComm) "@credo-ts/askar": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/anoncreds": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/openid4vc": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/react-native": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/tenants": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/cheqd": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/indy-vdr": "^0.6.0" "@openwallet-foundation/askar-react-native": "^0.4.0" (replaces @hyperledger/aries-askar-react-native) "@hyperledger/anoncreds-react-native": "^0.2.4" "@hyperledger/indy-vdr-react-native": "^0.2.2" "@credo-ts/core": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/didcomm": "^0.6.0" (new, required if using DIDComm) "@credo-ts/askar": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/anoncreds": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/openid4vc": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/node": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/tenants": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/cheqd": "^0.6.0" "@credo-ts/indy-vdr": "^0.6.0" "@openwallet-foundation/askar-nodejs": "^0.4.0" (replaces @hyperledger/aries-askar-nodejs) "@hyperledger/anoncreds-nodejs": "^0.2.4" "@hyperledger/indy-vdr-nodejs": "^0.2.2"

This section will list all breaking changes made to the public API of Credo between version 0.5.x and 0.6.x. info If you have custom modules take into account there could be a lot more breaking changes that aren't documented here. We try to make sure that the biggest breaking changes to the internal API are also documented here, but it is possible some breaking changes are not documented here (feel free to open a pull request).

Credo 0.6.0 is now a pure ESM package. It cannot be require()'d from CommonJS. Since Node 20.19 you may be able to require() ESM modules. However, we strongly recommend moving to ESM instead. If your project is a Node.js application, you will need to migrate it to ESM or use a Node.js version that supports requiring ESM modules (Node.js 22+). The recommended approach is to migrate your project to ESM: Add "type": "module" to your package.json. Replace all require() / module.exports with import / export. Use only full relative file paths for imports: import x from './index.js' instead of import x from '.'. Use the node: protocol for Node.js built-in imports (e.g. import fs from 'node:fs'). If using TypeScript, add "module": "node16" and "moduleResolution": "node16" to your tsconfig.json. You must use a .js extension in relative imports even though you're importing .ts files. Replace usages of __dirname and __filename with import.meta.dirname and import.meta.filename (Node.js 20.11+), or use import.meta.url with fileURLToPath. If your project is a React Native application, this change should not impact you since React Native uses its own bundler (Metro) which handles ESM syntax. tip For a comprehensive guide on migrating a CommonJS project to ESM, see Pure ESM package by Sindre Sorhus.

Starting from Credo 0.6, Node 18 has been deprecated. The supported versions are Node 20 and 22. We aim to keep support for all LTS releases that are either Current, Active, or in Maintenance. See the Release Schedule on the Node.js website for information on past and upcoming Node.js releases.

One of the most significant changes in Credo 0.6.0 is that all DIDComm-related functionality has been extracted from @credo-ts/core into a new @credo-ts/didcomm package. This means: If your application does not use DIDComm at all, you simply need to remove DIDComm-related settings from your Agent configuration. No @credo-ts/didcomm dependency is needed. If your application does use DIDComm, you need to add @credo-ts/didcomm to your dependencies and update your imports and agent setup. The following subsections cover all the DIDComm-related breaking changes. Agent setup with DIDComm​ Previously, DIDComm modules (connections, credentials, proofs, mediation, etc.) were automatically included in the agent. Now you must explicitly include them using the getDefaultDidcommModules() helper, and settings like endpoints are passed through DIDComm module configuration instead of the main agent config. 0.5.x 0.6.x import { Agent } from '@credo-ts/core' import { agentDependencies } from '@credo-ts/node' import { HttpInboundTransport, HttpOutboundTransport } from '@credo-ts/node' const agent = new Agent({ config: { label: 'My Agent', endpoints: ['https://myendpoint.com'], walletConfig: { id: 'my-wallet', key: 'my-wallet-key', }, }, dependencies: agentDependencies, modules: { /* ... other modules */ }, }) agent.registerInboundTransport(new HttpInboundTransport({ port: 3000 })) agent.registerOutboundTransport(new HttpOutboundTransport()) import { Agent } from '@credo-ts/core' import { agentDependencies } from '@credo-ts/node' import { getDefaultDidcommModules, DidCommHttpInboundTransport, DidCommHttpOutboundTransport, } from '@credo-ts/didcomm' const agent = new Agent({ config: { // label and endpoints have been removed from config }, dependencies: agentDependencies, modules: { ...getDefaultDidcommModules({ endpoints: ['https://myendpoint.com'], }), /* ... other modules */ }, }) agent.didcomm.registerInboundTransport(new DidCommHttpInboundTransport({ port: 3000 })) agent.didcomm.registerOutboundTransport(new DidCommHttpOutboundTransport()) DIDComm API access pattern​ All DIDComm-related module APIs are now scoped under agent.didcomm instead of being accessed directly on agent. 0.5.x 0.6.x const defaultMediator = await agent.mediationRecipient.findDefaultMediator() const proofRecord = await agent.proofs.getById(proofRecordId) const credentialRecord = await agent.credentials.getById(credentialRecordId) const oobRecord = await agent.oob.createInvitation() const connections = await agent.connections.getAll() const defaultMediator = await agent.didcomm.mediationRecipient.findDefaultMediator() const proofRecord = await agent.didcomm.proofs.getById(proofRecordId) const credentialRecord = await agent.didcomm.credentials.getById(credentialRecordId) const oobRecord = await agent.didcomm.oob.createInvitation() const connections = await agent.didcomm.connections.getAll() DIDComm class prefix changes​ Most DIDComm-related classes, events and services now use the DidComm prefix in their naming. Imports must be updated from @credo-ts/core to @credo-ts/didcomm. 0.5.x 0.6.x import { AgentMessage, ConnectionsModule, MediatorPickupStrategy, HttpInboundTransport, HttpOutboundTransport, WsInboundTransport, WsOutboundTransport, ConnectionEventTypes, CredentialEventTypes, ProofEventTypes, } from '@credo-ts/core' import { DidCommMessage, DidCommConnectionsModule, DidCommMediatorPickupStrategy, DidCommHttpInboundTransport, DidCommHttpOutboundTransport, DidCommWsInboundTransport, DidCommWsOutboundTransport, DidCommConnectionEventTypes, DidCommCredentialEventTypes, DidCommProofEventTypes, } from '@credo-ts/didcomm' DIDComm-related event type strings have also changed to distinguish them from events triggered by other protocols. Credentials / Proofs API normalization​ The DIDComm credentials and proofs APIs have been updated for consistency. In particular, credentialExchangeRecord is now used instead of credentialRecord and proofExchangeRecord instead of proofRecord in method parameters. 0.5.x 0.6.x const requestedCredentials = await agent.proofs.selectCredentialsForRequest({ proofRecordId: proofRecord.id, }) await agent.proofs.acceptRequest({ proofRecordId: proofRecord.id, proofFormats: { anoncreds: requestedCredentials.proofFormats.anoncreds }, }) const requestedCredentials = await agent.didcomm.proofs.selectCredentialsForRequest({ proofExchangeRecordId: proofRecord.id, }) await agent.didcomm.proofs.acceptRequest({ proofExchangeRecordId: proofRecord.id, proofFormats: { anoncreds: requestedCredentials.proofFormats.anoncreds }, }) Dropped label and connectionImageUrl from agent configuration​ The label and connectionImageUrl fields have been removed from the main Agent configuration. They are not present as a general DIDComm configuration parameter either. If you need to use them, you can specify them per-call in DIDComm connection establishment methods: const outOfBandRecord = await agent.didcomm.oob.createInvitation({ label: 'My Agent', imageUrl: 'https://myhost/myimage.png', }) await agent.didcomm.oob.receiveInvitation(invitation, { label: 'My Agent', imageUrl: 'https://myhost/myimage.png', }) tip If you need to persist these values and your only persistent storage is the agent's wallet, you can use Generic Records to store arbitrary data. DID Exchange defaults changed to did:peer:4​ Up to Credo 0.5.x, the default did:peer method used for DID Exchange was did:peer:1. In 0.6.0, the default is now did:peer:4. If you are interacting with older agents that don't support this method, you can override this setting in the DIDComm connections module configuration: import { DidCommConnectionsModule, PeerDidNumAlgo } from '@credo-ts/didcomm' const agent = new Agent({ modules: { ...getDefaultDidcommModules({ endpoints: ['https://myendpoint.com'] }), connections: new DidCommConnectionsModule({ peerNumAlgoForDidExchangeRequests: PeerDidNumAlgo.GenesisDoc, }), }, }) Inbound/Outbound transports configuration​ Transports are now registered through the agent.didcomm API or as part of the DIDComm module configuration, instead of on the agent instance directly. 0.5.x 0.6.x import { HttpInboundTransport, HttpOutboundTransport } from '@credo-ts/node' agent.registerInboundTransport(new HttpInboundTransport({ port: 3000 })) agent.registerOutboundTransport(new HttpOutboundTransport()) import { DidCommHttpInboundTransport, DidCommHttpOutboundTransport, } from '@credo-ts/didcomm' // Option 1: Register transports after agent creation agent.didcomm.registerInboundTransport(new DidCommHttpInboundTransport({ port: 3000 })) agent.didcomm.registerOutboundTransport(new DidCommHttpOutboundTransport()) Alternatively, transports can be specified directly in the DidCommModule configuration through the transports property, which is especially useful in React Native apps or when you want to keep all configuration in one place: import { DidCommModule, DidCommHttpInboundTransport, DidCommHttpOutboundTransport, } from '@credo-ts/didcomm' const agent = new Agent({ modules: { didcomm: new DidCommModule({ transports: { inbound: [new DidCommHttpInboundTransport({ port: 3000 })], outbound: [new DidCommHttpOutboundTransport()], }, }), }, }) MessagePickupRepository → QueueTransportRepository​ If you are creating a DIDComm mediator or a related extension module, MessagePickupRepository has been refactored to QueueTransportRepository and now belongs to DIDComm module configuration. The MessagePickupRepository injection symbol has been dropped. To retrieve the current QueueTransportRepository instance, resolve DidCommModuleConfig and access queueTransportRepository. All methods in QueueTransportRepository now include AgentContext as their first argument. Deprecated DIDComm protocols​ The following DIDComm protocols and formats are marked as deprecated in 0.6.0. The Connection, V1 Credential and V1 Proof protocols are still available in 0.7 and are removed in 0.8. The Legacy Indy formats still work with the V2 protocols in 0.8. Connection Protocol V1 — Update to the DID Exchange protocol instead. V1 Credential Protocol — Update to the V2 Credential Protocol instead. Legacy Indy Credential Format — Update to the AnonCreds Credential Format. V1 Proof Protocol — Update to the V2 Proof Protocol instead. Legacy Indy Proof Format — Update to the AnonCreds Proof Format. Express v5​ If you're using the DIDComm HTTP transports or the OpenID4VC issuer/verifier packages, you should update to Express v5 (express@^5.0.0).

The walletConfig property has been removed from the main InitConfig. Instead, each module defines its own storage and KMS configuration. For Askar, there is a new store property on the AskarModule config where you set the wallet id and key. 0.5.x 0.6.x import { Agent } from '@credo-ts/core' import { AskarModule } from '@credo-ts/askar' import { ariesAskar } from '@hyperledger/aries-askar-nodejs' const agent = new Agent({ config: { label: 'My Agent', walletConfig: { id: 'my-wallet', key: 'my-wallet-key', }, }, modules: { askar: new AskarModule({ ariesAskar }), }, }) import { Agent } from '@credo-ts/core' import { AskarModule } from '@credo-ts/askar' import { askar } from '@openwallet-foundation/askar-nodejs' const agent = new Agent({ config: { // walletConfig removed from here }, modules: { askar: new AskarModule({ askar, store: { id: 'my-wallet', key: 'my-wallet-key', }, }), }, })
documents.s: Wallet configuration removed from agent config

documents.t: The wallet API has been completely rewritten. The previous agent.wallet API is replaced by the new agent.kms API. This new KMS supports multiple backends, symmetric keys, generic encryption/decryption, and identifies keys by key ID rather than by public key. Key changes: Key and Jwk classes removed — replaced by the new PublicJwk class. JwaSignatureAlgorithm renamed — use Kms.KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms instead. agent.wallet removed — use agent.kms for all key management operations. Wallet injection symbol removed — if you used this in custom modules, inject the KMS API using agentContext.resolve(Kms.KeyManagementApi) instead. 0.5.x 0.6.x import { JwaSignatureAlgorithm, KeyType } from '@credo-ts/core' const key = await agent.wallet.createKey({ keyType: KeyType.Ed25519 }) const publicKeyBase58 = key.publicKeyBase58 const algorithm = JwaSignatureAlgorithm.EdDSA import { Kms } from '@credo-ts/core' const { keyId, publicJwk } = await agent.kms.createKey({ type: 'ed25519' }) const algorithm = Kms.KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.EdDSA

When signing with DIDs in Credo, it is now required that all DIDs have an associated DidRecord with the created role. The new KMS API needs to track key IDs for keys within a DID document, and these are stored on the DID record. You can import a DID using agent.dids.import and provide the keys array to define the mapping between verification method and key ID. If a verification method mapping is not provided, Credo assumes the legacy key ID format (base58 encoded public key).

Credential records have been updated to support batch credentials and KMS key tracking. record.credential is now record.firstCredential storeCredential() has been replaced by store() which expects a record parameter 0.5.x 0.6.x await agent.w3cCredentials.storeCredential({ credential }) const credential = record.credential const record = W3cCredentialRecord.fromCredential(credential) await agent.w3cCredentials.store({ record }) const credential = record.firstCredential Records now support multiple credential instances via the credentialInstances array and a multiInstanceState property to track usage.

The Askar native bindings have been moved from @hyperledger to @openwallet-foundation scope. 0.5.x 0.6.x import { ariesAskar } from '@hyperledger/aries-askar-nodejs' // or import { ariesAskar } from '@hyperledger/aries-askar-react-native' import { askar } from '@openwallet-foundation/askar-nodejs' // or import { askar } from '@openwallet-foundation/askar-react-native'

The default typ header for SD-JWT VCs has been changed from vc+sd-jwt to dc+sd-jwt. You can still use vc+sd-jwt by providing the headerType value when signing an SD-JWT VC. For OID4VCI, the typ header is based on the OID4VCI credential format used.
documents.s: SD-JWT VC typ header default changed

documents.t: The BBS+ module has been removed. The underlying implementation was outdated and unmaintained. A new version based on the BBS standard currently being developed may be added in the future. If you still need the legacy BBS+ functionality, you can extract the code from an older commit of the Credo repository and create your own custom module.
Support for DIDComm linked attachments has been removed. The functionality was not working correctly and only supported the deprecated V1 issuance protocol.

The @credo-ts/indy-sdk-to-askar-migration package has been removed. The Indy SDK has been deprecated for a long time, and all wallets should have been migrated to Askar by now. If you haven't migrated yet, first update to 0.5.x and then to 0.6.x.

The automatic backup functionality has been removed from Credo. With the generalization of the KMS API and moving away from assuming Askar is used for storage, providing a generic backup API is not feasible. From now on, you are expected to create backups yourself before performing any updates.

TypeScript target updated to ES2020 — this generally should not impact supported environments (Node.js / React Native). Uint8Array instead of Buffer — internal key bytes representation now uses Uint8Array instead of Buffer. Uncompressed keys by default — EC keys (P-256, P-384, P-521, K-256) now default to uncompressed representation. Zod 4 — Credo has been updated to Zod 4. Although the public API has not changed, error messages and some error structures may differ. DidCommV2Service renamed — DidCommV2Service is now LegacyDidCommV2Service, and NewDidCommV2Service became the default DidCommV2Service. Modules no longer experimental — DcqlModule, DifPresentationExchangeModule, SdJwtVcModule, MdocModule, TenantsModule, CheqdModule, DrpcModule, OpenId4VcModule, and X509Module are no longer experimental. createDeviceResponse returns bytes — createDeviceResponse now returns raw Uint8Array bytes instead of a base64-encoded string. DidDocumentService.protocolScheme() removed — this method has been removed as it's not possible to determine the protocol scheme from the base class.

The X509Certificate API has been updated to better support key management: The async getData() method has been split into a sync .data getter and an async getThumbprint() method. APIs that involve signing now require X509Certificate instances instead of encoded certificate strings. This allows you to attach a keyId to the certificate before passing it. When signing with an X509 certificate, a keyId must always be set on the certificate instance. For certificates created before 0.6, use the legacy key id format. For certificates created after 0.6, you must manually store the key id and re-attach it after decoding. // For certificates created before 0.6 const certificate = X509Certificate.fromEncodedCertificate(encodedCert) certificate.keyId = certificate.publicJwk.legacyKeyId // For certificates created after 0.6 (store the keyId yourself) const certificate = X509Certificate.fromEncodedCertificate(encodedCert) certificate.keyId = myStoredKeyId Self-signed certificate creation is now done via agent.x509.createCertificate where the subjectPublicKey is not supplied or is equal to the authorityKey.

The three separate OpenID4VC modules have been merged into a single OpenId4VcModule. The old OpenId4VcHolderModule, OpenId4VcIssuerModule, and OpenId4VcVerifierModule are replaced by OpenId4VcModule, which accepts optional issuer and verifier configuration. The holder is always available. The router property on OpenId4VcIssuerModule and OpenId4VcVerifierModule has been replaced by a top-level app property on OpenId4VcModule. You pass your Express app instance directly, and Credo registers all routes (including .well-known paths) on it. If no app is provided and either issuer or verifier is configured, a new Express app instance is created automatically. caution Register your custom routes after calling agent.initialize() to ensure Credo's routes are registered first and your custom middleware does not clash with Credo's routes. 0.5.x 0.6.x import express from 'express' import { OpenId4VcHolderModule, OpenId4VcIssuerModule, OpenId4VcVerifierModule } from '@credo-ts/openid4vc' const issuerApp = express() const verifierApp = express() const agent = new Agent({ modules: { openId4VcHolder: new OpenId4VcHolderModule(), openId4VcIssuer: new OpenId4VcIssuerModule({ baseUrl: 'https://issuer.example.com', router: issuerRouter, credentialRequestToCredentialMapper: async ({ credentialRequest }) => { /* ... */ }, }), openId4VcVerifier: new OpenId4VcVerifierModule({ baseUrl: 'https://verifier.example.com', router: verifierRouter, }), }, }) // Register routers manually issuerApp.use('/oid4vci', issuerRouter) verifierApp.use('/oid4vp', verifierRouter) // Access holder API await agent.modules.openId4VcHolder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer) // Access issuer API await agent.modules.openId4VcIssuer.createIssuer() // Access verifier API await agent.modules.openId4VcVerifier.createVerifier() import express from 'express' import { OpenId4VcModule } from '@credo-ts/openid4vc' const app = express() const agent = new Agent({ modules: { openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule({ app, issuer: { baseUrl: 'https://issuer.example.com', credentialRequestToCredentialMapper: async ({ credentialRequest }) => { /* ... */ }, }, verifier: { baseUrl: 'https://verifier.example.com', }, }), }, }) // Holder is always available await agent.openid4vc.holder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer) // Issuer API (only available if issuer config was provided) await agent.openid4vc.issuer.createIssuer() // Verifier API (only available if verifier config was provided) await agent.openid4vc.verifier.createVerifier()

The requestCredentials method on the holder now returns objects with a record property (a W3cCredentialRecord, SdJwtVcRecord, or MdocRecord), pre-populated with KMS key IDs. Store each received credential using the store({ record }) method on the appropriate credential API. 0.5.x 0.6.x const credentialsResult = await agent.modules.openId4VcHolder.requestCredentials({ resolvedCredentialOffer, ...accessTokenResponse, credentialBindingResolver: () => ({ method: 'did', didUrls: [holderDid] }), }) for (const credential of credentialsResult.credentials) { await agent.w3cCredentials.storeCredential({ credential: credential.credential }) } const credentialsResult = await agent.openid4vc.holder.requestCredentials({ resolvedCredentialOffer, ...accessTokenResponse, credentialBindingResolver: () => ({ method: 'did', didUrls: [holderDid] }), }) for (const credential of credentialsResult.credentials) { if (credential.record instanceof W3cCredentialRecord) { await agent.w3cCredentials.store({ record: credential.record }) } else if (credential.record instanceof SdJwtVcRecord) { await agent.sdJwtVc.store({ record: credential.record }) } else if (credential.record instanceof MdocRecord) { await agent.mdoc.store({ record: credential.record }) } }

The credentialBindingResolver is now called once for the entire credential request (instead of once per credential). It can return multiple keys or a single key attestation to support batch issuance scenarios.
documents.s: OpenID4VCI credential binding resolver called once

documents.t: The method for resolving an authorization code flow request has been renamed: 0.5.x 0.6.x await agent.modules.openId4VcHolder.resolveIssuanceAuthorizationRequest( resolvedCredentialOffer, authCodeFlowOptions ) await agent.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VciAuthorizationRequest( resolvedCredentialOffer, authCodeFlowOptions )

The version strings for credential offer versions have been updated. Draft 15 is incompatible with previous drafts, so if you are interacting with older issuers or holders you need to keep this in mind. 0.5.x 0.6.x v1.draft11-13 v1.draft11-15 v1.draft13 v1.draft15 V1 support has also been added (v1) which is the default.

Support for SIOPv2 has been removed. All classes, interfaces, and services that had Siop in their name have been renamed to use OpenId4Vp. For example, OpenId4VcSiopHolderService is now OpenId4VpHolderService. Update all imports accordingly.

The default responseMode when creating an authorization request has changed from direct_post (unencrypted) to direct_post.jwt (encrypted). If you need to revert to unencrypted responses (e.g., for interoperability with older agents), you can set the responseMode explicitly: await agent.openid4vc.verifier.createAuthorizationRequest({ verifierId, requestSigner: { /* ... */ }, presentationExchange: { /* ... */ }, responseMode: 'direct_post', // opt out of encryption })
documents.s: OpenID4VP responseMode default changed to direct_post.jwt

documents.t: The field in returned credential entries from DIF Presentation Exchange results has been renamed from type to claimFormat to better align with the DC API terminology. 0.5.x 0.6.x const verifiedResponse = await agent.modules.openId4VcVerifier.verifyAuthorizationResponse({ /* ... */ }) for (const submission of verifiedResponse.presentationExchange.presentations) { console.log(submission.type) // e.g. 'dc+sd-jwt' } const verifiedResponse = await agent.openid4vc.verifier.verifyAuthorizationResponse({ /* ... */ }) for (const submission of verifiedResponse.presentationExchange.presentations) { console.log(submission.claimFormat) // e.g. 'dc+sd-jwt' }
documents.s: OpenID4VP DIF Presentation Exchange credential entry type → claimFormat

documents.t: DCQL query results have changed: the selected credentials per query are now an array of credential IDs (at least one entry) instead of a single presentation. This allows the multiple option in DCQL queries to be properly supported.
documents.s: OpenID4VP DCQL multiple presentations per query

documents.t: Per ISO 18013-7, only one mDOC document per OpenID4VP device response is now supported. If a device response contains multiple documents, each is verified separately. When creating a device response for OpenID4VP presentation, ensure you only include one document.
documents.s: OpenID4VP mDOC: only one document per device response

documents.t: Support for creating authorization requests using the x509_san_uri client id scheme has been removed from the verifier/issuer side (the holder still supports receiving such requests). This scheme is replaced by x509_hash in newer drafts, which is supported via the x509_hash client id prefix.
documents.s: OpenID4VP x509_san_uri client id scheme removed on verifier side

This guide lists what you need to change to update an agent from Credo 0.6 to 0.7: dependencies, breaking changes, and deprecated APIs to replace before 0.8. Read Updating Credo first for the general steps. Most breaking changes landed in 0.7.0 and 0.7.1. Credo 0.7.2 adds a PKCE security fix for the OpenID4VC issuer and the import paths this guide uses, so update straight to 0.7.2 or later. caution Back up your storage before you update. Credo doesn't create backups for you.

Update every @credo-ts/* package to ^0.7.2. All Credo packages must have the same version. Then update the native libraries you use: Library 0.6 0.7 Askar (@openwallet-foundation/askar-*) ^0.4.3 0.6.1 (@credo-ts/askar accepts ^0.4.3 || ^0.5.0 || ^0.6.0) AnonCreds (@hyperledger/anoncreds-*) ^0.3.4 ^0.4.0 Indy VDR (@hyperledger/indy-vdr-*) ^0.2.3 ^0.3.0 The new native versions load their libraries with koffi instead of ffi-napi. Use the same version for the -nodejs, -react-native and -shared package of a library: for example askar-nodejs@0.6.1 depends on exactly askar-shared@0.6.1. With mixed versions, npm installs a second copy of askar-shared for @credo-ts/askar, and the agent fails to start with Native askar has not been registered yet. If you use @credo-ts/askar-to-drizzle-storage-migration, it requires exactly @openwallet-foundation/askar-shared@0.6.0. For example, for an agent with Askar and AnonCreds: Node.js React Native npm pnpm yarn bun npm install \ @credo-ts/core@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/node@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/askar@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/anoncreds@^0.7.2 \ @openwallet-foundation/askar-nodejs@0.6.1 \ @hyperledger/anoncreds-nodejs@^0.4.0 pnpm add \ @credo-ts/core@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/node@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/askar@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/anoncreds@^0.7.2 \ @openwallet-foundation/askar-nodejs@0.6.1 \ @hyperledger/anoncreds-nodejs@^0.4.0 yarn add \ @credo-ts/core@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/node@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/askar@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/anoncreds@^0.7.2 \ @openwallet-foundation/askar-nodejs@0.6.1 \ @hyperledger/anoncreds-nodejs@^0.4.0 bun add \ @credo-ts/core@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/node@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/askar@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/anoncreds@^0.7.2 \ @openwallet-foundation/askar-nodejs@0.6.1 \ @hyperledger/anoncreds-nodejs@^0.4.0 The minimum Node.js version is still 20.19, but Credo 0.7 is tested on Node.js 22 and 24, and 0.8 requires Node.js 22. npm pnpm yarn bun npm install \ @credo-ts/core@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/react-native@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/askar@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/anoncreds@^0.7.2 \ @openwallet-foundation/askar-react-native@0.6.1 \ @hyperledger/anoncreds-react-native@^0.4.0 \ @dr.pogodin/react-native-fs pnpm add \ @credo-ts/core@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/react-native@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/askar@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/anoncreds@^0.7.2 \ @openwallet-foundation/askar-react-native@0.6.1 \ @hyperledger/anoncreds-react-native@^0.4.0 \ @dr.pogodin/react-native-fs yarn add \ @credo-ts/core@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/react-native@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/askar@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/anoncreds@^0.7.2 \ @openwallet-foundation/askar-react-native@0.6.1 \ @hyperledger/anoncreds-react-native@^0.4.0 \ @dr.pogodin/react-native-fs bun add \ @credo-ts/core@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/react-native@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/askar@^0.7.2 \ @credo-ts/anoncreds@^0.7.2 \ @openwallet-foundation/askar-react-native@0.6.1 \ @hyperledger/anoncreds-react-native@^0.4.0 \ @dr.pogodin/react-native-fs Credo now prefers @dr.pogodin/react-native-fs over the unmaintained react-native-fs. Both still work, and you need one of them.

Credo 0.7 doesn't change the storage format, so you don't need to run the update assistant. If you use Drizzle, apply the new SQL migrations. Credo 0.7 adds migrations for the core and openid4vc bundles.
The members of LogLevel are now PascalCase. Their numeric values didn't change. // 0.6 new ConsoleLogger(LogLevel.debug) // 0.7 new ConsoleLogger(LogLevel.Debug)

Credo no longer uses the buffer package. All APIs take and return Uint8Array, and @credo-ts/core no longer exports Buffer, Uint8ArrayBuffer, AnyUint8Array and base64ToBase64URL. Values that used to be a Buffer, such as the result of TypedArrayEncoder.fromBase64, are now a plain Uint8Array, so Buffer methods like toString('base64') don't work on them. Use TypedArrayEncoder instead. Several encoder methods were renamed: 0.6 0.7 TypedArrayEncoder.fromString TypedArrayEncoder.fromUtf8String TypedArrayEncoder.toBase64URL TypedArrayEncoder.toBase64Url JsonEncoder.toBase64URL JsonEncoder.toBase64Url JsonEncoder.toString / JsonEncoder.fromString JsonEncoder.toUtf8String / JsonEncoder.fromUtf8String JsonEncoder.toBuffer / JsonEncoder.fromBuffer JsonEncoder.toUint8Array / JsonEncoder.fromUint8Array TypedArrayEncoder.fromBase64 and JsonEncoder.fromBase64 no longer accept base64url input. Use the new fromBase64Url methods for that. // 0.6 import { Buffer, JsonEncoder, TypedArrayEncoder } from '@credo-ts/core' const seed = TypedArrayEncoder.fromString('my-seed') const payload = JsonEncoder.fromBase64(base64UrlString) // 0.7 import { JsonEncoder, TypedArrayEncoder } from '@credo-ts/core' const seed = TypedArrayEncoder.fromUtf8String('my-seed') const payload = JsonEncoder.fromBase64Url(base64UrlString) TypedArrayEncoder.equals now runs in constant time. DIDComm attachments are now encoded as base64url. Credo decodes both base64 and base64url attachments, but if you read attachment.data.base64 yourself, use attachment.getDataAsJson() or attachment.getDataAsUint8Array(), which accept both.

Use findVerificationMethodsByTypeAndPurpose on the DID document. It returns all matching verification methods, in the order of the relationships you pass. To keep the old behavior, pass the relationships the old function searched: // 0.6 const verificationMethod = await findVerificationMethodByKeyType('Ed25519VerificationKey2018', didDocument) // 0.7 const [verificationMethod] = didDocument.findVerificationMethodsByTypeAndPurpose('Ed25519VerificationKey2018', [ 'verificationMethod', 'authentication', 'keyAgreement', 'assertionMethod', 'capabilityInvocation', 'capabilityDelegation', ]) findVerificationMethodsByPurpose(purposes) does the same without filtering on type.

validityInfo.validUntil is now required when you sign an mdoc, with agent.mdoc.sign or Mdoc.sign, and for every mdoc you return from the OpenID4VC issuer's credentialRequestToCredentialMapper: // 0.6 await agent.mdoc.sign({ docType, namespaces, holderKey, issuerCertificate }) // 0.7 await agent.mdoc.sign({ docType, namespaces, holderKey, issuerCertificate, validityInfo: { validUntil: new Date('2027-01-01') }, }) Signing throws when validFrom is before signed (which defaults to now), or when validUntil isn't later than validFrom. Two more mdoc changes from 0.7.1: Elements in the deviceSigned part of a device response must be authorized in the mdoc. Authorize them at signing time with the new keyAuthorizations option. A CWT status list referenced by an mdoc must have an expiration time, so pass expiresAt when you create one, and its sub must equal the URI it's referenced by.

These changes need no code changes, but credentials and presentations that verified with 0.6 can now be rejected: SD-JWT: a compact SD-JWT must end with ~, disclosure salts must be unique, and the sub of a status list token must equal the uri that references it. COSE: signing a Sign1 or Mac0 structure fails when no algorithm is declared. It no longer falls back to the first algorithm the key supports. JSON-LD: Ed25519Signature2018 only accepts Ed25519VerificationKey2018 verification methods, and Ed25519Signature2020 requires Ed25519VerificationKey2020. ldp_vp presentations: the signer of the presentation must control the credentialSubject.id of each credential, as Credo already required for jwt_vp and SD-JWT. The result is in credentials[].credentialSubjectAuthentication. Generic JSON-LD verification rejects anoncreds-2023 proofs. Those are verified through the AnonCreds module. OpenID4VC: JWTs signed with a DID, such as signed authorization requests, key attestations, wallet attestations and signed issuer metadata, are now checked against getTrustedIssuersForVerification when you configure it. Before, only JWTs signed with an X.509 certificate were checked.

InMemoryLruCache now keeps separate entries per agent context. This fixes entries being shared between tenants. RedisCache stores entries that are shared between contexts under a global: prefix. Existing entries for those caches are missed once after the update. Custom Cache implementations receive an optional CacheOptions argument on get, set and remove. When scope is 'global', share the entry between all agent contexts. Otherwise, which must be the default, keep it per agentContext.contextCorrelationId. // 0.7 import type { AgentContext, Cache, CacheOptions } from '@credo-ts/core' class MyCache implements Cache { public async get<CacheValue>( agentContext: AgentContext, key: string, options?: CacheOptions ): Promise<CacheValue | null> { const scope = options?.scope ?? 'context' // look up `key` globally, or for agentContext.contextCorrelationId } // set(agentContext, key, value, expiresInSeconds?, options?) and remove(agentContext, key, options?) }

Before 0.7.1, the defaultBackend option of the key management module was ignored, and the first backend that supported an operation was used. Credo now uses the default backend when you don't pass backend, and only falls back to another backend, with a warning, when the default one doesn't support the operation. If you set defaultBackend, check that new keys end up in the backend you expect.

DIDs created with Credo before 0.7.1 don't resolve anymore. A bug in how earlier versions of didwebvh-ts calculated hashes made them incompatible with the spec. Attested resources are now signed with a key that the DID references from assertionMethod. New DIDs include that reference. For existing DIDs, add it with agent.dids.update and republish the DID log before you sign resources with them.

Credo 0.7.2 fixes a security issue in the authorization code flow: the issuer now stores the code_challenge of a pushed authorization request or authorization challenge request, and checks the code_verifier against it at the token endpoint. A token request with a code_verifier but no matching code_challenge is rejected with invalid_grant. Only the S256 method is supported. The new pkceRequired option rejects authorization requests without a code_challenge, as FAPI 2.0, HAIP and OAuth 2.1 require. It defaults to false in 0.7 and to true in 0.8. Enable it now: new OpenId4VcModule({ issuer: { baseUrl: 'https://issuer.example.com/oid4vci', pkceRequired: true, credentialRequestToCredentialMapper, }, }) You can override it per issuance session with authorization.requirePkce in createCredentialOffer, or requirePkce in getDynamicIssuanceSession. An explicit requirePkce: false turns PKCE off for that session. authorization.requireDpop and authorization.requireWalletAttestation in createCredentialOffer are now optional. In 0.7, leaving them out and setting them to false both mean "use the global setting". In 0.8, false turns the requirement off for the session, so leave them out instead of passing false.

For the presentation during issuance flow, resolveOpenId4VciAuthorizationRequest now returns a codeVerifier when the authorization server supports PKCE. Pass it to requestToken, otherwise issuers that check PKCE, such as Credo 0.7.2 and later, reject the token request: const authorizationRequest = await agent.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VciAuthorizationRequest( resolvedCredentialOffer, authCodeFlowOptions ) // Present the requested credentials to authorizationRequest.openid4vpRequestUrl, then: const { authorizationCode } = await agent.openid4vc.holder.retrieveAuthorizationCodeUsingPresentation({ resolvedCredentialOffer, authSession: authorizationRequest.authSession, presentationDuringIssuanceSession, }) await agent.openid4vc.holder.requestToken({ resolvedCredentialOffer, code: authorizationCode, clientId, codeVerifier: authorizationRequest.codeVerifier, })
The APIs below still work in 0.7. Replace them now: the ones marked "removed in 0.8" are gone in the next version.

Import the AnonCreds DIDComm formats and protocols from @credo-ts/anoncreds/didcomm, and the AnonCreds registries of cheqd, Hedera and did:webvh from the /anoncreds subpath of their package. These subpaths need 0.7.2 or later. // 0.6 import { AnonCredsDidCommCredentialFormatService, LegacyIndyDidCommCredentialFormatService } from '@credo-ts/anoncreds' import { CheqdAnonCredsRegistry } from '@credo-ts/cheqd' import { HederaAnonCredsRegistry } from '@credo-ts/hedera' import { WebVhAnonCredsRegistry } from '@credo-ts/webvh' // 0.7 import { AnonCredsDidCommCredentialFormatService, LegacyIndyDidCommCredentialFormatService } from '@credo-ts/anoncreds/didcomm' import { CheqdAnonCredsRegistry } from '@credo-ts/cheqd/anoncreds' import { HederaAnonCredsRegistry } from '@credo-ts/hedera/anoncreds' import { WebVhAnonCredsRegistry } from '@credo-ts/webvh/anoncreds' AnonCredsModule and the other non-DIDComm AnonCreds APIs stay in @credo-ts/anoncreds.

The W3C Data Integrity credential format (Aries RFC 0809) moved to @credo-ts/didcomm, because it isn't specific to AnonCreds. AnonCredsModule registers the AnonCreds link secret binding for it, so you don't need to configure anything else. // 0.6 import { DataIntegrityDidCommCredentialFormatService } from '@credo-ts/anoncreds' new DidCommCredentialV2Protocol({ credentialFormats: [new DataIntegrityDidCommCredentialFormatService()] }) // 0.7 import { DidCommCredentialV2Protocol, DidCommDataIntegrityCredentialFormatService } from '@credo-ts/didcomm' new DidCommCredentialV2Protocol({ credentialFormats: [new DidCommDataIntegrityCredentialFormatService()] }) The AnonCreds Data Integrity names in @credo-ts/core were renamed as well: Deprecated Replacement DataIntegrityProof AnonCredsW3cCredentialProof DataIntegrityProofOptions AnonCredsW3cCredentialProofOptions ANONCREDS_DATA_INTEGRITY_CRYPTOSUITE ANONCREDS_W3C_CREDENTIAL_CRYPTOSUITE IAnonCredsDataIntegrityService IAnonCredsW3cCredentialService AnonCredsDataIntegrityServiceSymbol AnonCredsW3cCredentialServiceSymbol AnoncredsDataIntegrityCreatePresentation AnonCredsW3cCredentialCreatePresentation AnoncredsDataIntegrityVerifyPresentation AnonCredsW3cCredentialVerifyPresentation W3cJsonLdVerifiableCredential.dataIntegrityCryptosuites W3cJsonLdVerifiableCredential.anonCredsW3cCredentialCryptosuites

The Connection protocol (RFC 0160), Issue Credential v1 and Present Proof v1 have been deprecated since 0.6 and are still available in 0.7. Move to DID Exchange and to DidCommCredentialV2Protocol and DidCommProofV2Protocol. The legacy Indy credential and proof formats work with the v2 protocols.

Pass the NativeAskar and NativeAnoncreds classes instead of the deprecated askar and anoncreds exports of the native packages. Credo then looks up the native library each time it uses it, so it no longer matters whether the native package was imported before Credo. This fixes errors such as Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'keyGetJwkSecret') in ESM, bundler and test runner setups. It needs 0.7.2 or later, and NativeAskar needs Askar 0.6.0. // 0.6 import { askar } from '@openwallet-foundation/askar-nodejs' import { anoncreds } from '@hyperledger/anoncreds-nodejs' new AskarModule({ askar, store: { id: 'my-wallet', key: 'my-key' } }) new AnonCredsModule({ anoncreds, registries: [new IndyVdrAnonCredsRegistry()] }) // 0.7 import { NativeAskar } from '@openwallet-foundation/askar-nodejs' import { NativeAnoncreds } from '@hyperledger/anoncreds-nodejs' new AskarModule({ askar: NativeAskar, store: { id: 'my-wallet', key: 'my-key' } }) new AnonCredsModule({ anoncreds: NativeAnoncreds, registries: [new IndyVdrAnonCredsRegistry()] }) Indy VDR has no native class, so keep passing indyVdr to IndyVdrModule.

getTrustedCertificatesForVerification on the X.509 module is replaced by getTrustedIssuersForVerification in the agent config. The new callback covers both X.509 certificate chains and DIDs, and takes precedence over the old one. Return undefined to fall back to the next source of trusted certificates, or an empty trustedIssuers list to trust nothing. // 0.6 new X509Module({ getTrustedCertificatesForVerification: async (agentContext, verificationContext) => [rootCertificate], }) // 0.7 new Agent({ config: { getTrustedIssuersForVerification: async (agentContext, { signer, verification }) => { if (signer.method !== 'x509') return undefined return { trustedIssuers: [{ method: 'x509', issuance: [rootCertificate] }] } }, }, // ... }) See Trusted issuers.

The issuer option allowDynamicIssuanceSessions is replaced by the getDynamicIssuanceSession callback, which also supports wallet-initiated issuance through a chained authorization server and presentation during issuance. This callback does what allowDynamicIssuanceSessions: true did: // 0.6 issuer: { allowDynamicIssuanceSessions: true /* ... */ } // 0.7 issuer: { getDynamicIssuanceSession: ({ origin, requestedCredentialConfigurations }) => { if (origin !== 'credentialRequest') return undefined return { authorizationFlow: 'external', credentialConfigurationIds: Object.keys(requestedCredentialConfigurations), } }, // ... }

SD-JWT VC and W3C SD-JWT: disclosing claims through disclosedPayload is deprecated in favor of disclosedPaths, which selectCredentialsForRequest fills in for you. applyDisclosuresForPayload is replaced by applyDisclosuresForPaths. mdoc: MdocDeviceResponse.createDeviceResponseWithDcqlQuery and MdocService.createDcqlQueryDeviceResponse are deprecated. Use DcqlService.createPresentation, or createDeviceResponse with explicit document requests.

Not required for the update, but worth knowing: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0, secured with JWT, SD-JWT or Data Integrity. w3cV2Credentials, w3cDataIntegrity and tokenStatusList are now default agent modules. See W3C Verifiable Credentials. Token Status Lists for SD-JWT VC and mdoc, including mdoc revocation. The ISO 18013-7 Annex C Digital Credentials API for mdoc. X.509 certificate revocation checks with CRLs. HPKE algorithms in the Askar and Node.js key management backends. connectionParameters for Askar on PostgreSQL, for example to configure SSL. Running the DIDComm HTTP inbound transport on an Express app you already have. The DIDComm W3C SD-JWT credential format (Aries RFC 0881).
